desc:
In-app and email notifications for SaaS apps tell users what matters without making them watch a screen. Ecom Swift LLC builds the bell icon, the alert list, the matching emails and the preference settings in your own product, written in plain, friendly words.

## What are in-app and email notifications?

In-app notifications are short messages shown inside your product, usually behind a bell icon with an unread count. Email notifications carry the same news to a user's inbox for events that happen while they are away. Together they let an app speak up when something needs attention, such as a finished export, a new comment or a usage limit being reached.

Without them, users must keep checking the dashboard to see whether anything changed. Many will simply forget.

## Why notifications keep users informed and engaged

A well-judged notification saves a user from missing something important and gives them a reason to return at the right moment. A finished report, an assigned task or a failed payment all call for a response, and the sooner the user knows, the sooner it is dealt with.

Too many messages, however, teach people to ignore all of them. That is why the design matters as much as the sending. Clear wording, a sensible choice of events and user control over what they receive keep notifications useful. Preferences, digests and quiet hours turn a stream of alerts into something people are glad to receive.

## What a good notification system includes

- A bell icon with an unread count in the app header.
- A list of recent alerts, with timestamps and links to the related item.
- Mark as read for one alert and for all at once.
- Matching emails for the events that need them.
- A branded email template that fits your product.
- A preferences page where users turn each type on or off.
- A daily or weekly digest for people who want fewer emails.
- Quiet hours, so messages wait until the working day starts.
- Rules that admins set for which events notify which roles.
- A delivery log that shows what was sent and opened.

## How we build it

We start by listing the events in your product that deserve a message, and for each one who should receive it, where, and with what wording. We also agree which should be in-app only, which also need email, and which can wait for a digest.

Then we build the notification store, the bell and list in your front-end, and the sending logic on your server. Emails go through the email service you already use or one you choose, with a template that matches your brand. The Basic package adds the bell, alert list and a few events. Standard adds email, a template, user preferences and a digest option. Premium adds scheduling, quiet hours, admin rules, a delivery log and a handover call. We test each event by triggering it and checking both the in-app message and the email.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Notify only for events a user can act on or wants to know about.
- Write messages in plain words that say what happened and what to do.
- Link each alert straight to the relevant item.
- Let users choose what they receive.
- Group busy activity into a digest.

**Avoid:**
- Sending an email for every minor event.
- Vague titles such as "Update available".
- Making notification settings hard to find.
- Marking everything urgent.
- Sending messages at night without quiet hours.

## Who this is for

This service suits SaaS teams whose users miss important events because nothing tells them. It suits a founder adding collaboration features such as comments and assignments, and a support-driven business that wants to cut "I didn't know" messages. It also fits apps with long-running jobs, where users want a message when the job finishes.

## What we need from you

Send a list of the events you want to announce, who should hear about each one, and any wording you already like. Tell us which email service you use and share your brand colors and logo.

Please add us as a collaborator on your code repository, so the alerts can be wired into your existing events. We never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until notifications are live.
